statement: Hana has a ribbon 40 cm long. She cuts off a fifth of it. How many centimetres of ribbon are left?

choices.misconception: I took away 5 cm, as if a fifth meant 5 centimetres.
I took away a quarter of the ribbon instead of a fifth.
I cut the ribbon in half instead of taking off a fifth.
I found the fifth that was cut off and gave that instead of the piece that is left.

hints: First find how long the piece that is cut off is.
A fifth means one of five equal parts. Find one part, then check whether the question asks for the piece cut off or the piece left.
One fifth of 40 cm is 40 divided by 5 = 8 cm. Take that away from the whole ribbon.

solutions.reliable: A fifth of 40 cm is 40 divided by 5 = 8 cm, so 40 - 8 = 32 cm are left. The transferable idea: find one equal part first, then read again whether the question wants the part taken or the part left.

whyOnTest: Finding a fraction of a quantity, here a fifth of a length, is one step, and the length of the piece cut off is offered as the trap.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
